---
title: "Antitrust Lab"
subtitle: "Interactive tools for competition economics"
---

Change the inputs, watch the outcome, and test the economics behind competition law. Each tool runs in your browser: no installation, no login. The first visit takes a little longer while the tool loads.

::: {.part}
## Markets and market power
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tool-grid">
  <div class="tool-card live">
    <h3>Monopoly and welfare</h3>
    <p class="q">What does monopoly cost society? Consumer and producer surplus, deadweight loss, and rent seeking.</p>
    <p class="meta">About 10 minutes</p>
    <a class="go" href="welfare/">Open the tool &rarr;</a>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card live">
    <h3>How many firms?</h3>
    <p class="q">Are more firms always better? Competition, fixed costs, and free entry.</p>
    <p class="meta">About 10 minutes</p>
    <a class="go" href="how-many-firms/">Open the tool &rarr;</a>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card live">
    <h3>Market definition</h3>
    <p class="q">Is this product a market of its own? SSNIP test, critical loss, and the cellophane fallacy.</p>
    <p class="meta">About 15 minutes</p>
    <a class="go" href="market-definition/">Open the tool &rarr;</a>
  </div>
  <div class="tool-card live">
    <h3>Concentration and market power</h3>
    <p class="q">How much market power do concentrated markets have? Lerner index, HHI and the merger screen, GUPPI.</p>
    <p class="meta">About 15 minutes</p>
    <a class="go" href="concentration/">Open the tool &rarr;</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.part}
